slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Now we can prove the Unit 2 constructions.

Perpendicular bisector: the arcs from A and B have equal radius, so the crossing points P and Q have PA = PB and QA = QB. First define M=PQ∩AB, with P and Q chosen on opposite sides of AB, and establish M lies between A and B. Then angle APQ=BPQ by SSS; because PM is ray PQ, angle APM=BPM. AP = BP and PM = PM, so triangles APM and BPM are congruent by SAS, giving AM = BM and equal angles at M that form a linear pair, so each is 90 degrees.

Angle bisector and angle copy: the equal arcs make two triangles congruent by SSS, and CPCTC gives the equal angles.
